sentences.text: Western Australia’s Corruption and Crime Commission brought together common legal principles and methods for use by reference in later misconduct reports.
sentences.support: set out those matters in a single section 88 report

sentences.text: It explained its jurisdiction, the meaning of misconduct and public officer, and rules governing reporting and disclosure.
sentences.support: The term “public officer” is defined in section 3 of the CCC Act

sentences.text: The Commission explained that it forms misconduct opinions using the civil standard of proof and does not determine criminal or disciplinary guilt.
sentences.support: the Commission does not determine whether any person has committed a criminal or disciplinary offence

sentences.text: It also described the opportunity for people and bodies to respond before adverse matters are reported.
sentences.support: the Commission must give the person or body a reasonable opportunity to make representations

findings.quote: The Commission may form an opinion as to misconduct on the evidence before it only if satisfied of misconduct on the balance of probabilities.

notes: No executive summary or equivalent findings overview is present. This report explains common legal and reporting principles; it does not investigate a particular allegation or make a numbered set of recommendations. Its legal descriptions are summarised as the Commission’s account in this report, not as current legal advice.
